slides.headline: NVIDIA WAS THE OBVIOUS BUYER. IT EVEN INVESTED FIRST.
slides.body: Nvidia already had a check in Decart's latest round, alongside Amazon. Reports had Nvidia close to finalizing the deal before someone showed up with a bigger number.

slides.headline: SPACEX IS PAYING $7 BILLION FOR A TEAM THAT LETS AI BUILD THE WORLD AROUND YOU
slides.body: Decart's AI generates the entire world from scratch, in real-time, as you move through it. The startup has 100 employees and raised at a $4 billion valuation just three months ago.

slides.headline: MUSK PLAYED THE GAME. TYPED 'WOW'. NEVER STOPPED THINKING ABOUT IT.
slides.body: In 2024, Musk tested OASIS and posted a single word on X: 'wow'. That post opened a direct line between him and Decart's CEO. The contact never stopped.

slides.headline: NVIDIA FUNDED THE STARTUP. THEN LOST IT TO A ROCKET COMPANY.
slides.body: Nvidia invested in Decart's $300 million round in May 2026. Then SpaceX walked in and bid nearly double. At $7 billion, that's roughly $70 million per employee.

slides.headline: MUSK ALREADY HAS XAI. SO WHY IS SPACEX THE ONE BUYING DECART?
slides.body: The $7 billion deal gives SpaceX, not xAI, direct control of Decart's real-time world-generation engine. It's the first sign Musk is embedding AI capability inside his aerospace company itself.

caption:
SpaceX is buying Israeli AI startup Decart for $7 billion because Musk played their game and typed 'wow' on X. 🧵

Musk tested OASIS, Decart's real-time AI video engine, in 2024, posted one word on X, and reportedly kept in contact with the team ever since. SpaceX is now in advanced talks to acquire the 100-person startup for up to $7 billion. Nvidia, which invested in Decart's $300 million round in May 2026 at a $4 billion valuation, was the frontrunner buyer before SpaceX reportedly outbid them. Decart was founded in 2023 by two Unit 8200 veterans and had raised over $450 million total. If the deal closes, SpaceX would have its first R&D presence in Tel Aviv.

Real-time AI that generates content on the fly, without a pre-built script, is now the most competed-over technology in the world. The same logic that stopped Musk mid-scroll in a video game already runs inside customer tools and live assistants that businesses deploy today. The companies moving first are running fully automated systems that handle questions, leads, and follow-up, set up once and running forever.
